in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you responsible for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This means do you live with him and are you the main person looking after him (paying for things like food, clothes, and childcare)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I live with him and I'm the one who looks after him day-to-day. I pay for all his needs like food, clothes, school things, everything really. It's just the two of us at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. It's clear you are responsible for Alex.

Now I need to ask: **Are you currently in the UK, and are you and Alex normally living in the UK? Also, do you have the right to reside in the UK (for example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, indefinite leave to remain, or another immigration status that allows you to live here)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we're both living in the UK - this is our home. I'm a UK citizen, so no issues there with right to reside or anything like that. We're not planning to move abroad or anything - we're settled here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or making a claim for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him, so no one else would be claiming for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You are responsible for him - you live together and you pay for all his needs
- You're both living in the UK
- You're a UK citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

All the eligibility criteria are met, so you can make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. You can apply online through the government's website, or by filling in a paper claim form if you prefer.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
